text:
alice: FYI seeing a sharp throughput drop in us-west around 08:13UTC. Lots of worker restarts and GPU OOMs, KV eviction rate jumped. Investigating now.

deploy-bot: :warning: alert created for cluster us-west-2 (incident id inc-181500).

infra-bot: Noted. Auto-scaling didn't kick due to reserve limits.

ben: Can you paste the OOM logs? suspect fragmentation or bad kernel fallback.

alice: Pasted log excerpt below:
```
[08:13:22] worker-17: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 536870912)
[08:13:23] runtime: KV evict shard=42 evicted=1.1GB total_evicted=3.7GB
[08:13:24] kernel_select: fallback to matmul_generic (workspace insufficient)
[08:13:24] scheduler: restart worker-17 (exit_code=137)
```

carol: Profiling snapshot shows kernel selector started choosing slower kernels after workspace checks increased by 3x. p50 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~860ms.

diego: GPU memory maps look fragmented. `nvidia-smi` shows lots of small allocations and persistent cuda contexts. Paste: 
```
GPU 0: 80% mem used (top processes: worker-12 10GB, worker-17 9.6GB, system-reserved 1GB)
But fragmentation metric (alloc_fail_count) spiking on multiple hosts.
```

emma: Batching heuristics also changed — saw the batching tuner reduce batch_size to 1 for many routes (latency SLOs), which increased per-token overhead and KV pressure. Might be a feedback loop: small batches -> more KV churn -> fragmentation -> OOM -> restarts.

ben: Agreed. Two hypotheses: 1) noisy tenant causing a burst of large-context requests (seq_len) forcing fallback kernels with larger workspace, fragmenting GPU memory. 2) a recent autotuner change that made batching too conservative for certain routes.

alice: Reproduced locally on a canary: sending many long-context requests to a single model instance triggers the same pattern — kernel_select chooses workspaceless variant after allocation check fails. Kernel switch increases temporary allocations.

runtime-bot: Flight recorder: matched metric spike: kv_evictions/sec 0.4 -> 8.9, worker_restarts/min 0 -> 4, p50_latency 0.12s -> 0.86s between 08:12:50-08:25:00.

carol: Uploading perf flame for the window (shortened): main hotspot: kernel_select -> matmul_generic -> cudaMemcpy (excess copying). Suggest we instrument workspace_estimate to log requested vs available.

diego: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) throttle per-tenant concurrent inflight to 10 on us-west, 2) force kernel selector to prefer low-fragmentation kernels (even if slightly slower) temporarily, 3) trigger KV compaction/eviction policy tuning.

emma: Also roll back batching autotuner change from yesterday in us-west canary. That one increased latency-safety thresholds too aggressively.

alice: Implemented 1) and 2) at 08:20. Commands run:
```
redwoodctl quota set --tenant heavy-tenant --concurrency 10 --region us-west-2
redwoodctl runtime set-kernel-preference --region us-west-2 --policy low-fragmentation
```

ben: Good. Any immediate signal?

runtime-bot: After mitigations: kv_evictions/sec dropped to 1.1, worker_restarts/min down to 0.6, p50 went to ~180ms by 08:32. Throughput recovered to ~92% of baseline by 08:36.

carol: We'll collect a full profiling trace and a root-cause doc. Possible follow-ups: - stronger kernel workspace accounting, - KV cache compaction during low load, - batching autotuner rollback + tighter canary.

alice: Agree. Opening follow-up tickets and scheduling a postmortem. Thanks everyone for the quick triage :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: incident inc-181500 marked 'mitigated' at 08:36 UTC.

diego: Note for postmortem: capture tenant request patterns (seq_len distribution) and correlate with kernel choices + workspace failures.

emma: I'll add a regression test that simulates long-context noisy tenants to the autotuner CI.

carol: Saving profiling artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-perf/incidents/1815004321/

alice: Closing from our side once postmortem is posted.
